testedBehaviors: Suspended child process assigned to a kill-on-job-close Job Object before resume.
Parent-death integration observes the execute child and its descendant terminate; reopening the queue marks the stale run failed and exposes no result or orphan artifact.
Queue close does not publish terminal state or artifacts before a live child is confirmed reaped.
Controlled ResumeThread, TerminateJobObject, WaitForSingleObject, and CloseHandle failures preserve live/owned-handle state until cleanup can be retried.
Queued/running cancel, forced timeout, access-denied, worker restart, terminal race, and partial-artifact isolation cases pass.
Express HTTP DELETE → worker RPC integration waits for the execution child to exit/reap before 200/cancelled; the test fixture's descendant exits and its delayed artifact stays absent.
limitations: Parent-death, child, and descendant behavior was exercised in this native Windows run; the injected WinAPI error cases use controlled mocks rather than inducing kernel API faults.

Queue.close has a bounded six-second join; these passing tests establish no premature terminal/artifact publication, not that close always returns only after every possible cleanup failure has resolved.
This suite does not exercise the full browser UI click-to-cancel-to-refresh-to-restore journey.
